note: Exact points only where a source gives one. NASA's Artemis candidate regions are broad areas (about 15 x 15 km); they are listed separately as regions, never as certified landing points.

sites.name: Outpost (simulated) — ridge site
sites.event: A fictional research outpost. The location is real and was chosen by code: the flattest-enough point within 25 km of the pole with the most long-term sunlight in NASA's 18.6-year illumination map, where Earth is up at least 30 % of the time.
sites.source: scripts/outpost.py — NASA PGDA product 69 map: sun 89.6 %, Earth 53.8 % (120 m pixel); slope 0.8 deg (LOLA 80 m).

sites.name: Survey point S-1 — the shadow problem
sites.event: 433 m from the outpost. Chosen by code as the nearby spot with the least long-term sunlight that is not permanently dark.
sites.source: scripts/outpost.py — NASA PGDA product 69 map: sun 11.3 %, Earth 0.1 %.

sites.name: Shadow Research Station (simulated)
sites.event: A fictional station on a real site chosen by code: flat ground with moderate long-term sunlight (45 %) right next to near-permanent shadow.
sites.source: scripts/bases.py — NASA PGDA 69 map: sun 45.0 %, Earth 54.4 %; slope 4.3° (LOLA 80 m).

sites.name: SH-2 — shadow survey point
sites.event: 865 m from the Shadow Station; NASA's 18.6-year map shows it almost never sunlit.
sites.source: scripts/bases.py — NASA PGDA 69 map: sun 1.4 %, Earth 45.6 %.

sites.name: EarthLink Communications Station (simulated)
sites.event: A fictional communications station on a real site chosen by code for Earth visibility (62 % long-term) with sunlight for power (65 %).
sites.source: scripts/bases.py — NASA PGDA 69 maps: Earth 61.9 %, sun 64.5 %; slope 4.1° (LOLA 80 m).

sites.name: LS-1 — Lost Signal site
sites.event: 1087 m from EarthLink: the nearby spot with the least long-term Earth visibility (0 %).
sites.source: scripts/bases.py — NASA PGDA 69 map: Earth 0.0 %, sun 0.0 %.

sites.name: IM-2 Athena — target point
sites.event: Intuitive Machines' Athena landed on 6 Mar 2025 about 250 m from this target, on its side inside a small crater; the mission ended the next day.
sites.source: LROC 'IM-2 Landing Region' (https://www.lroc.asu.edu/images/1401): target about 84.78 S, 29.13 E on Mons Mouton.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus — landing site
sites.event: Intuitive Machines' Odysseus landed on 22 Feb 2024 about 1.5 km from Malapert A and tipped over; it operated until about 29 Feb 2024, as night reached the site.
sites.source: Landing location 80.13 S, 1.44 E as verified by NASA's LROC team (reported by SpaceNews and Benzinga, Feb 2024).

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram — Statio Shiv Shakti
sites.event: ISRO's Vikram landed on 23 Aug 2023; ISRO put it to sleep at 02:30 UTC on 4 Sep 2023, 'a little before sunset', and it did not wake up.
sites.source: IAU-approved Statio Shiv Shakti, 69.373 S, 32.319 E (Wikipedia, citing the IAU WGPSN, Mar 2024).

sites.name: Near the south pole (0 E, 89.5 S)
sites.event: A reference point 15 km from the pole, used in the Horizons checks.
sites.source: Chosen test coordinate (not a landing site).

sites.name: Apollo 11 — Tranquility Base
sites.event: First crewed landing, 20 Jul 1969 (Mare Tranquillitatis). EVA 2.53 h, 0.25 km traverse, 21.55 kg of samples (NSSDC). Crew: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the surface; Michael Collins in lunar orbit.
sites.source: Lunar Module position from NASA NSSDC 'Apollo Landing Sites' (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/lunar_sites.html); mission facts from NSSDC 'Apollo Lunar Landings'. Terrain: LOLA global 118 m DEM.

sites.name: Apollo 15 — Hadley-Apennine
sites.event: Landed 30 Jul 1971 at Hadley Rille, beneath the Apennine mountains; first mission with the Lunar Roving Vehicle. EVA 19.13 h, 27.9 km traverse, 77.31 kg of samples (NSSDC). Crew: David Scott and James Irwin on the surface; Alfred Worden in orbit.
sites.source: NSSDC 'Apollo Landing Sites' and 'Apollo Lunar Landings'. Terrain: LOLA global 118 m DEM.

sites.name: Apollo 17 — Taurus-Littrow
sites.event: Last crewed landing, 11 Dec 1972, in the Taurus-Littrow valley between massifs. EVA 22.07 h, 35 km traverse, 110.52 kg of samples (NSSDC). Crew: Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt on the surface; Ronald Evans in orbit.
sites.source: NSSDC 'Apollo Landing Sites' and 'Apollo Lunar Landings'. Terrain: LOLA global 118 m DEM.

regions.source: NASA, 'NASA Provides Update on Artemis III Moon Landing Regions' (Oct 2024). NASA lists nine regions near the south pole; it does not publish single landing points, so the app shows their names only.

reference.name: Apollo 11 — Tranquility Base
reference.event: First crewed landing, 20 Jul 1969 (Mare Tranquillitatis). EVA 2.53 h, 0.25 km traverse, 21.55 kg of samples (NSSDC). Crew: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the surface; Michael Collins in lunar orbit.
reference.source: Lunar Module position from NASA NSSDC 'Apollo Landing Sites' (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/lunar_sites.html); mission facts from NSSDC 'Apollo Lunar Landings'. Terrain: LOLA global 118 m DEM.
